title: P418 fully coupled flow--heat step-response extension
purpose: Quantify the error introduced by fixing velocity, pressure and face mass flux during thermal-step prediction, using the same published P418 endpoint pairs as the main thermal-response study.
source_title: Pore-scale simulation on flow and heat transfer characteristics in packed beds with internal heat sources at low Reynolds numbers
initial_state_rule: Use the source condition's converged steady-iteration-200 internal U, p, p_rgh, phi, fluid-temperature and solid-temperature fields. The label 200 is a steady iteration index, not physical seconds.
target_rule: At t=0 switch only the one declared inlet velocity, inlet temperature or solid volumetric heat-source input to the exact target P418 endpoint. The inlet phi boundary values are copied from that same target endpoint so the imposed inlet U, T and mass flux are mutually consistent; internal and outlet flow fields remain at the source state. Retain the registered outlet pressure, cooling-wall temperature, geometry and material properties.
time_step_rule: The existing finest thermal schedule is only the first fully coupled pilot. A representative velocity step must be repeated at three temporal resolutions before the fully coupled histories are accepted; differences in U, p, temperature, wall heat and mass/energy balance are reported directly.

time_step_sensitivity.formal_execution_rule: The twelve formal curves can start only after the representative summary has the declared fully-coupled status, velocity-step id, three time steps and finest staged schedule matching the first 25 s of the formal 300 s plan.

sequence_rule: Use exactly the same twelve source--target endpoint pairs and complete-curve data splits as the quasi-steady-hydrodynamic thermal study.

input_preparation.rule: The source endpoint supplies every internal U, p, p_rgh, phi and T value. The exact target pore-opening velocity, inlet/backflow temperature, inlet phi boundary values and volumetric heat-source dictionary are applied from t=0. No internal or outlet flow field is replaced by the target steady state.

openfoam_execution.restart_rule: Resume only from the latest time at which U, p, p_rgh, phi and T exist for every MPI rank and both regions contain their required state.
openfoam_execution.workstation_pause_rule: If the cloud-migration pause marker exists, execution stops unless ALLOW_PAUSED_WORKSTATION_RUN=1 is given explicitly.

data_export.rule: Every saved time retains U, p, fluid/solid T and oriented internal/boundary face mass flux; fixed-hydrodynamics curves remain a separate data mode.

fixed_vs_fully_coupled_comparison.rule: Compare the same twelve sequence ids over common recorded times. Report dimensional and fully-coupled-response-normalized differences for each engineering history without imposing a fitted acceptance percentage.

model_extension.deterministic_model: regional graph--Transformer predicting time-dependent U, p and T plus conservative face mass flux
physics_relations: predicted face mass flux consistency with reconstructed rho U dot S
model_extension.physics_scale_rule: Keep all equations dimensional in the finite-volume module and calculate positive residual scales from complete training curves only. Return equation-wise terms separately rather than hiding fixed relative weights.
model_extension.diffusion_role: If used later, diffusion corrects the residual after the deterministic full-state model and must not alter prescribed boundary values or material properties.
model_extension.implementation_status: full-state and face-flux forward model, continuity, momentum, dual-region energy, interface and rho-U-face-flux consistency relations, projection-aware losses, complete-curve training, validation selection and restart have passed a small end-to-end run; formal training waits for accepted fully coupled OpenFOAM histories

scientific_scope: This extension tests flow--thermal coupling for the same fixed packing and published endpoint families. It does not introduce buoyancy, pebble motion, thermo-mechanical deformation, accident conditions or new material parameters.
